stories.narrative:
## Narrative: Bluepeak incident retro — 2026-10-10

**The incident and its shape.** On Monday 2026-10-05, Bluepeak's search was degraded for three hours and forty-one minutes, from 9:12am to 12:53pm.

The deploy that went out at 9:12am introduced the bad configuration; the error budget burn alert fired at 9:15am, three minutes later.

The root cause was the **config partition**: the deploy shipped a config that split query traffic unevenly across the search shards, and one shard saturated.

The initial investigation blamed the search index and sent the team chasing a reindex for the first forty minutes — Aisha pushed the team to check the config diff instead, which is where the real cause was found.

Mitigation was a rollback of the config to the previous partition at 12:40pm; traffic normalized within thirteen minutes and search was fully healthy by 12:53pm.

Customer-facing comms: first status posted at 9:40am, all-clear at 1:05pm, written by Sam from customer engineering with Aisha.

**SLO and contractual state.** The search SLO is 99.9 percent; the month landed at 99.86, so the SLO was breached.

Bluepeak was offered a service credit and their account team accepted it.

**Committed follow-ups (durable, owned, dated).** Two actions were chosen to prevent this class of incident, both proposed by Nora:
- **Pre-deploy check comparing partition weights against the shard capacity model** — owned by **Maya**, due **2026-11-02**.

- **Make the config diff visible in the deploy review** — owned by **Diego**, due **2026-11-09**.

Additionally, the **search team will run a shard capacity review before the end of the year**, with **Priya** volunteering to lead it.

**What went well.** The rollback went smoothly because the deploy tooling kept the previous config one click away.

The on-call stayed calm — the team's own view is that this matters more than any tooling.

**Publication policy (durable org rule).** The retro is published **company-wide**.

Incident writeups are **opt-out by default** — a decision taken after the August incident — so the whole company sees the timeline and follow-ups.

A retro room is booked for Friday morning for anyone who wants to talk it through.

**Reasoning carried forward.** The config-diff visibility action is directly supported by the investigation's failure mode: the index was blamed first and cost forty minutes, so making the diff legible at review time attacks the actual detection gap.

The pre-deploy partition check attacks the cause itself (uneven traffic split vs.

shard capacity).

The shard capacity review is the broader structural follow-up — it questions whether the capacity model the pre-deploy check will lean on is itself current.
